full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN.** I found a close match to this exact system in a very recent preprint. My confidence is medium, because I could only read secondary summaries of that preprint.

**1. Model family.**
This is a two-species reaction-diffusion (Turing) system with cross-taxis. The kinetics are the Sel'kov glycolysis model in the same form as Schnakenberg-type activator-depletion kinetics. I checked this against the prompt's equations: u' = -u + a·v + u²v and v' = b - a·v - u²v, with steady state u = b and v = b/(a+b²). D2/D1 = 1000 gives a strong Turing regime. The terms c1·div(u∇v) and c2·div(v∇u) are chemotaxis-like (nonlinear cross-diffusion) fluxes. The standard name is "reaction–diffusion–chemotaxis" or "reaction–cross-diffusion" Turing pattern formation.

**2. The specific behaviour.**
The behaviour is a non-monotonic effect of taxis strength: pattern amplitude rises then falls to uniform, and spots turn into stripes as |c| grows. The closest source is Karmakar & Basu (2026), a Sel'kov model with chemotaxis between its two species.
- A Pith review of the long paper, "Chemotaxis-induced linear instabilities and pattern formation in a reaction-diffusion model", says the study covers linear instabilities and pattern formation in a spatially extended Selkov model for glycolysis with diffusion and chemotactic interactions between two species.
- The same page says the results show chemotaxis can act as a nonmonotonic control parameter for wavelength selection, re-entrant pattern formation and pattern morphology.
- A second Pith page, "Nonmonotonic control of pattern formation by chemotaxis", is the companion short paper. It says numerical simulations of a chemotactic version of the Selkov glycolysis model show pattern amplitudes tracking the predicted curve and reveal chemotaxis-driven spot-to-stripe transitions.
- Pith's reading of the long paper says reciprocal chemotaxis gives uniform-to-pattern-to-uniform sweeps while extreme nonreciprocal chemotaxis yields pattern-to-uniform-to-pattern sweeps. I could not tell which of these sign conventions matches the opposite-sign sweep (c1 = c, c2 = -c) here. Check this against the primary text.
- It also says the spot-stripe transition is attributed to nonlinear effects beyond linear stability.

**Background that is earlier or more general.** None of these studies the spot-to-stripe sweep or the rise-and-fall of amplitude with taxis strength.
- Madzvamuse, Ndakwo & Barreira (2015), *J. Math. Biol.* 70:709–743, "Cross-diffusion-driven instability for reaction-diffusion systems: analysis and simulations". This is the venue as given by the ProQuest record; the Springer page's metadata says 2014 (online 27 March 2014). It treats linear cross-diffusion in activator-depleted kinetics (Gierer–Meinhardt, Schnakenberg).
- Madzvamuse, Barreira & Gerisch, "Cross-Diffusion in Reaction-Diffusion Models: Analysis, Numerics, and Applications" (Springer, Mathematics in Industry vol. 26). Its abstract describes a review of model equations, mathematical analysis, with an emphasis on pattern formation and positivity preservation. I did not confirm its year or exact bibliographic details.
- Chen et al. (2021), *Chaos* 31, "Pattern formation of reaction-diffusion system with chemotaxis terms". Its conclusion is that chemotaxis can give rise to pattern formation for the same diffusion coefficients.
- "Pattern formation arising from diffusive instability under random versus directed spatial motion", *Proc. R. Soc. A* 481 (2025). It shows chemotaxis may induce the Turing instability (if the chemotaxis gradient is strong enough).
- Gambino, Lombardo & Sammartino, nonlinear cross-diffusion Turing work (cited from memory). I did not retrieve it, so I do not rely on it.

**3. Caveats on verification.**
- I could not open the Karmakar–Basu preprint itself. The Pith pages are AI-generated reviews, and the second one cites it as "Associated long paper (2026)". The venue is therefore unverified; treat it as a 2026 preprint.
- I did not confirm the exact parameters (a = 0.015, b = 10, D2 = 1000·D1). I also did not confirm the numbers c ≈ 0.17 for the sharpest pattern and ≈ 0.49 for the uniform state. The qualitative behaviour matches, so the numbers are likely system-specific.
- Linear cross-diffusion in Schnakenberg is a different, older and well-studied variant. Its terms are linear (∇²-type) rather than div(u∇v), so I treat it only as background.

**Confidence: medium.** The model is nearly identical and the qualitative behaviour matches: non-monotonic amplitude, a re-entrant sequence and spot-to-stripe transitions. The medium rating is because I read only secondary summaries, and the sign convention is unconfirmed.
